outcomes.evidence: NCBI GeneReviews『Hereditary Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus』Molecular Pathogenesis: vasopressin binds collecting-duct V2 receptor, activates cAMP/PKA, and inserts AQP2 into luminal membrane, increasing water permeability. Therefore high osmolality with ADH secretion promotes water reabsorption and concentrated urine; answer index 4.
outcomes.caveat: Hereditary disorder reference confirms molecular pathway, not full normal renal physiology context. All 5 choice-by-choice independent evidence and 264-question regeneration pending.

outcomes.evidence: NCBI StatPearls『Physiology, Aldosterone』directly distinguishes aldosterone-driven distal sodium reabsorption/potassium excretion from ADH-driven aquaporin mobilization and water reabsorption. High potassium stimulates aldosterone, high osmolality stimulates ADH; answer index 0.
outcomes.caveat: Multiple hormonal regulators and individual kidney pathologies not ruled out; full 5-choice verification pending.

outcomes.evidence: NCBI StatPearls『Physiology, Thyroid』: anterior-pituitary TSH promotes thyroid T3/T4 synthesis, while high T3/T4 exert negative feedback and decrease TSH. Low TSH and high free T4 are consistent with feedback, not etiology determination; answer index 1.
outcomes.caveat: Low TSH/high free T4 has multiple etiologies; clinical diagnostic tests and full 5-choice independent proof pending.

outcomes.evidence: NCBI Bookshelf『Histology, Thyroid Gland』separately identifies follicular thyrocytes as thyroid hormone (T3/T4) producers regulating metabolism, and parafollicular C cells as calcitonin-producing cells involved in calcium homeostasis; answer index 2.
outcomes.caveat: Adult calcium regulation is primarily PTH/vitamin D and calcitonin has limited physiologic weight; preserve distinction. Full five-choice independent proof pending.
